nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of NiFe LDH/CNTs
nodes.procedure: The α-Ni_{2/3}Fe_{1/3}(OH)_2/CNTs composite was prepared via a hydrothermal process.
nodes.source_text: The α-Ni_{2/3}Fe_{1/3}(OH)_2/CNTs composite was prepared via a hydrothermal process and then was oxidized with H₂PtCl₆.

nodes.name: Pt oxidation anchoring (12h)
nodes.procedure: The α-Ni_{2/3}Fe_{1/3}(OH)_2/CNTs composite was oxidized with H₂PtCl₆ for 12 hours, during which Fe^{2+} was oxidized to trivalent state, Fe extravasated forming FeOOH clusters creating Fe cationic vacancies, and Pt was reduced and in situ anchored at the vacancies.
nodes.source_text: The samples oxidized for 12, 24, and 36h were denoted as Pt-Ni₂Fe₁·12, Pt-Ni₂Fe₁·24, and Pt-Ni₂Fe₁·36, respectively.

nodes.name: Pt oxidation anchoring (24h)
nodes.procedure: The α-Ni_{2/3}Fe_{1/3}(OH)_2/CNTs composite was oxidized with H₂PtCl₆ for 24 hours, during which Fe^{2+} was oxidized to trivalent state, Fe extravasated forming FeOOH clusters creating Fe cationic vacancies, and Pt was reduced and in situ anchored at the vacancies.
nodes.source_text: The samples oxidized for 12, 24, and 36h were denoted as Pt-Ni₂Fe₁·12, Pt-Ni₂Fe₁·24, and Pt-Ni₂Fe₁·36, respectively.

nodes.name: Pt oxidation anchoring (36h)
nodes.procedure: The α-Ni_{2/3}Fe_{1/3}(OH)_2/CNTs composite was oxidized with H₂PtCl₆ for 36 hours, during which Fe^{2+} was oxidized to trivalent state, Fe extravasated forming FeOOH clusters creating Fe cationic vacancies, and Pt was reduced and in situ anchored at the vacancies.
nodes.source_text: The samples oxidized for 12, 24, and 36h were denoted as Pt-Ni₂Fe₁·12, Pt-Ni₂Fe₁·24, and Pt-Ni₂Fe₁·36, respectively.

nodes.name: Ni4Fe1 oxidative anchoring
nodes.procedure: α-Ni_{4/5}Fe_{1/5}(OH)_2 was oxidized with H₂PtCl₆ for 24 hours to load Pt single atoms.
nodes.source_text: Lowering the content of Fe in α-Ni_{4/5}Fe_{1/5}(OH)_2 led to a reduced Pt loading of ≈5.15 wt% (named Pt-Ni4Fe1-24)

nodes.name: Oxygen oxidation (24h)
nodes.procedure: NiFe hydroxides with Fe vacancies were prepared by oxygen oxidation for 24 hours.
nodes.source_text: For comparison, NiFe hydroxides with Fe vacancies prepared by oxygen oxidation for different durations were denoted as v_{Fe}-Ni₂Fe₁-T (T represents the oxidization time).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows two-dimensional structure of Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscope (TEM) image of Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24 in Figure 1a indicates the two-dimensional structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes of ≈0.24 nm corresponding to the (015) planes of α-Ni₂/₃Fe₁/₃(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice fringes of ≈0.24 nm observed by the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) in Figure 1b correspond to the (015) planes of α-Ni₂/₃Fe₁/₃(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED patterns index the (015), (018), (110), (113) planes of α-Ni₂/₃Fe₁/₃(OH)₂ and (120) patterns of FeOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The top-right inset of Figure 1b presents the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns of Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24, indexing the (015), (018), (110) and (113) planes of α-Ni₂/₃Fe₁/₃(OH)₂, and the (120) patterns of FeOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected STEM shows atomically dispersed Pt single atoms on the surface of NiFe hydroxides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1c, the atomically dispersed Pt sites were observed on the surface of NiFe hydroxides.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping certifies uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, Pt, O, and C elements with Pt single atoms uniformly loaded.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectroscopy mapping in Figure 1d for Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24 certifies the distribution of Ni, Fe, Pt, O, and C elements, suggesting that Pt single atoms were uniformly loaded in the hydroxide nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES measures Pt content of ≈6.15 wt% in Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high content of Pt (≈6.15 wt%) was further measured by the inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ FTIR of CO adsorption shows peak at 2115 cm⁻¹ corresponding to CO adsorption at Ptδ⁺, confirming positively charged isolated Pt atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the in situ FTIR spectra of CO adsorption in Figure S2, Supporting Information, the atomic-scale Pt atoms in Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24 are all positively charged. The peak at 2115 cm⁻¹ corresponds to the CO adsorption at Ptδ⁺.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p shows Ni²⁺ 2p₃/₂ at 855.0 eV, Ni³⁺ 2p₃/₂ at 856.3 eV with Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ ratio ≈0.34 for Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24; Fe 2p peaks shift to lower binding energies; Pt 4f shows dominant Pt(II); O 1s shows metal-oxygen bonds at 530.3 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As observed in Figure 2a(i), the peaks located at ≈855.0 and ≈872.6 eV for vFe-Ni₂Fe₁-24 are assigned to Ni²⁺ 2p₃/₂ and Ni²⁺ 2p₁/₂ respectively... The Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ ratio of the as-prepared samples was calculated to be 0.34 for Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows peak at g=2.16 for Fe³⁺ with lower density in Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24 indicating Pt occupies Fe vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S4, Supporting Information shows electron paramagnetic resonance spectra of as-prepared composites and the peak at g = 2.16 corresponds to Fe³⁺ with an octahedral structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface areas are 100.11, 101.52, 111.28 m²g⁻¹ and pore volumes are 0.26, 0.27, 0.33 cm³g⁻¹ for Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-12, -24, -36 respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The resulting Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface areas of Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-12, Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24, and Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-36 are 100.11, 101.52, and 111.28 m²g⁻¹, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge and Ni K-edge XANES show electronic structure changes with lower Fe valence and higher Ni valence in Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24; FT-EXAFS shows Fe-O at 1.95 Å (N=5.6), Ni-O (N=5.8), reduced metal-metal coordination indicating vacancies; Pt L3-edge confirms isolated Pt-O at 1.6-1.7 Å with no Pt-Pt coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe K-edge of Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24 shows a slight shift to lower photon energy, and the Ni K-edge displays slightly positive shift... The only peak of Pt-O at 1.6–1.7 Å is observed in the EXAFS spectra of Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24, which implies that Pt atoms are present in an isolated state.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl = 2.23 mF cm⁻² for Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24 (vs 1.90 mF cm⁻² for vFe-Ni₂Fe₁-24), indicating increased ECSA from Pt single atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl of 2.23 mF for Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24 is larger than that of vFe-Ni₂Fe₁-24 (1.90 mF) and α-Ni₂/₃Fe₁/₃(OH)₂ (1.50 mF), demonstrating that Pt significantly increases the active surface area.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24 has the smallest charge transfer resistance Rct indicating good charge transfer kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt-Ni₂Fe₁-24 has the smallest charge transfer resistance (Rct), indicating good charge transfer kinetics.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns similar to previous NiFe hydroxides with disappearance of Pt peaks indicating high Pt dispersity and single-atom state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, all the XRD patterns of NiFe hydroxide-based samples in Figure S1, Supporting Information are similar to those of the previous NiFe hydroxides. The disappearance of Pt peaks in the XRD patterns suggests the high dispersity of Pt and even the possible single-atom state.
